== Biography ==

The Cheshire Cat is a creature of Wonderland, distinguished by its distinctive grin and capacity for speech. It appears good-natured in demeanor, though its very long claws and great many teeth suggest it ought to be treated with due respect.

Alice first becomes aware of the Cheshire Cat when she observes a curious appearance in the air. After watching it briefly, she makes out the form to be a grin and identifies it as the Cheshire Cat. The Cat converses with Alice, answering her questions about which way she ought to go.

The Cheshire Cat's presence in the court of Wonderland attracts considerable attention and becomes the subject of dispute. A large crowd gathers around it, and a controversy erupts among the executioner, the King, and the Queen, all speaking at once concerning the Cat's fate. The King expresses disapproval of the Cat's appearance, though he permits the Cat to kiss his hand if it wishes.

Alice handles the Cheshire Cat by tucking it under her arm.

== Narrative role ==

The Cheshire Cat encounters Alice in Wonderland while seated upon a tree branch. The creature is striking in appearance: though it seems good-natured, it has very long claws and a great many teeth, which inspire Alice to believe it should be treated with respect. When Alice asks for direction, the Cat answers with measured philosophy: "That depends a good deal on where you want to get to."

The Cat manifests to Alice again in an extraordinary manner. Where Alice perceives only a curious appearance in the air, she eventually recognizes it as a grin belonging to the Cheshire Cat. The creature speaks—"How are you getting on?"—though the words emerge only once there is sufficient mouth for speech. Alice, pleased by this companionship, introduces the Cheshire Cat to the King as her friend.

The Cat's presence attracts considerable commotion at court. A dispute erupts between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, all speaking at once regarding this creature. Alice is called upon to settle the question, though the clamor makes it difficult for her to discern what exactly is being argued. The matter remains unresolved when the disembodied cat's head disappears entirely.

== Personality ==

The Cheshire Cat is defined most strikingly by its perpetual grin. Alice first recognizes it by this feature alone—watching a curious appearance in the air resolve into "a grin"—and it greets her by grinning when their eyes meet. This constant expression gives it an air of good humor; Alice thinks it "looked good-natured," and it engages her readily in conversation, asking "How are you getting on?" as though they were old acquaintances resuming talk.

Yet the Cat possesses a reflective quality beneath its cheerful exterior. When Alice asks which way she ought to go, it responds with measured philosophy: "That depends a good deal on where you want to get to." The remark suggests an entity accustomed to thinking about matters of purpose and direction—not a mere animal, but something capable of reasoning about ends and means.

The Cat's physical form creates an interesting tension with its amiable nature. Though good-natured, it bears very long claws and a great many teeth—features that strike Alice as requiring respect. She does not fear it, yet she recognizes its potential for harm, and feels its nature warrants a certain caution. This combination of genial manner and formidable appearance makes the Cat an enigmatic presence.

The creature seems to draw attention wherever it goes, gathering crowds of onlookers from the court—executioner, King, and Queen all converge upon it, caught in some dispute over its very existence or disposition. That it provokes such fervent debate among Wonderland's authorities suggests it is either remarkable in its nature or peculiarly resistant to simple categorization.

== Appearance ==

The Cheshire Cat appears in Wonderland through a most peculiar manifestation. Rather than appearing whole, it first materializes as a grin in the air, a curious sight that gradually becomes the creature's full form as one watches.

Once fully manifest, the Cat possesses very long claws and a great many teeth. Despite these fearsome features, Alice found it to appear good-natured, though these apparent contradictions compelled her to regard the creature with appropriate respect.

The Cat is defined by its perpetual grin, which it displays frequently when it sees Alice. This smile remains its most characteristic feature throughout its encounters in Wonderland.

The Cheshire Cat has been observed perching upon the boughs of trees, and it possesses the ability to escape or vanish if not carefully held—a quality that became apparent when Alice held it under her arm to prevent its escape.

== Powers ==

The Cheshire Cat manifests in unusual fashion, appearing first as nothing more than a grin suspended in the air before its fuller form becomes visible. It possesses the faculty of speech and engages in reasoned dialogue, offering counsel such as the observation that one's proper path depends greatly on one's destination.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — friend. Alice regards the Cheshire Cat as someone to talk to and introduces it to the King as "a friend of mine." She seeks out the Cat for further conversation, returning to its side for continued discussion.

'''[[King]]''' — The King expresses disapproval of the Cat's appearance, saying "I don't like the look of it at all," though he permits the creature to kiss his hand if it wishes. The relationship appears distant and reserved.

'''[[Queen]]''' — The Queen involves herself in disputes concerning the Cat within the royal court, suggesting a contentious relationship.

== Trivia ==

* The Cheshire Cat's grin sometimes manifests in advance of its complete form, creating an extraordinary appearance suspended in the air before the rest of the creature becomes visible.
* The creature favors tree boughs as a perch, from which it observes passersby with its characteristic grin.
* Alice found the Cat sufficiently small to tuck under her arm during her adventures in Wonderland, suggesting a diminutive stature despite its formidable claws and teeth.
